# Fixture corpus

Assets for engine tests. Authored for this project, so there is no licensing
question, and deliberately **not** only well-behaved files.

`5-assets.md` §61 is the rule being followed: _"é importante incluir arquivos
ruins. O objetivo do corpus é encontrar problemas."_

---

## `svg/` — hand-authored

| fixture                            | what it is                                                     | which rule it exercises                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `simple.svg`                       | geometry only                                                  | `pure-vector` baseline                                                                                       |
| `gradient.svg`                     | `linearGradient` in `defs`                                     | gradient must not be treated as a risk on its own                                                            |
| `mask.svg`                         | `mask` + `maskUnits=userSpaceOnUse`                            | `complex-vector`, risk `mask`                                                                                |
| `filter.svg`                       | `feGaussianBlur` **with** `color-interpolation-filters="sRGB"` | the correct case                                                                                             |
| `filter-linear-rgb.svg`            | `feColorMatrix` **without** it                                 | `filter-without-srgb-interpolation` — the one transform `safe` may always apply                              |
| `raster-wrapper.svg`               | one `<image>`, no paths                                        | `raster-wrapper`, and explicitly **not** `invalid`                                                           |
| `mixed.svg`                        | 2 paths + 1 `<image>`                                          | `mixed`                                                                                                      |
| `external-reference.svg`           | `<style>` + remote `href`                                      | `external-resource`; optimising it "successfully" ships a file that renders blank                            |
| `text.svg`                         | live `<text>`                                                  | `text-dependent-rendering`; `text → path` must be opt-in                                                     |
| `broken-reference.svg`             | `fill="url(#does-not-exist)"`                                  | reference integrity is a **validation error**, not a warning                                                 |
| `no-viewbox.svg`                   | no `viewBox`                                                   | `removeDimensions` would destroy it                                                                          |
| `redundant-precision.svg`          | coordinates at 7 decimals                                      | does `safe` reduce precision at all, and does it move geometry                                               |
| `complex.svg`                      | **4 000 redundant nodes**                                      | multipass cost and per-node analysis                                                                         |
| `logo-imaginizim-{dark,light}.svg` | **the repo's own logos**                                       | real Figma exports: `filterUnits="userSpaceOnUse"`, `feColorMatrix` drop-shadow chains, absolute coordinates |

The two logos are the most valuable fixtures here. They are real, they are
the project's own, and they are exactly the shape that the current SVGO config
is most likely to damage — `convertColors`, `collapseGroups`, `mergePaths`
and `minifyStyles` all run over a Figma filter chain today.

`complex.svg` and `redundant-precision.svg` are generated by
`scripts/make-fixtures.mjs`. Regenerate with:

```bash
node scripts/make-fixtures.mjs
```

A 313 KB blob checked into the repo would tell you nothing about what it is
meant to prove; the generator says exactly that.

## `raster/` — copied from this repo's own `public/`

`pwa-192x192.png`, `pwa-maskable-192x192.png`, `logo-dark.png`, `logo.png`,
`og-image.png`, `readme-home-preview.png`.

Real files, project-owned, and already shipped — so they are guaranteed to
survive a rebuild.

### Known gap: no WebP, AVIF or JPEG fixtures

The repo contains no `.webp`, `.avif` or `.jpg` outside `public/`
(SVGO only bundles `.webp` inside its own test data, and it is minified).

That matters because the quality gate in slice 3 compares rendered output, and
the codec tests in slice 4 need inputs that actually decode as those formats.
Producing them by hand in Node is not feasible without adding a codec
dependency purely for fixtures, which is the wrong trade.

The honest way to close it: **encode the fixtures once, with the app's own
encoder, and commit the output.** Playwright is already a dependency, so the
generator can run `createImageBitmap` → `OffscreenCanvas.convertToBlob({type})`
inside a real browser and write real files. Not yet written — recorded here so
it does not quietly become a surprise in slice 3.

Also missing, and wanted by `5-assets.md` §61: JPEG repeatedly recompressed,
PNG with an unused alpha channel, PNG that is really a palette, WebP
losslessly encoded that should be lossy. These need the same generator plus a
deliberate composition step.

## Not here yet

The SVG fixtures are **strings on disk**, not registered with a loader. Nothing
in `src/` reads this directory yet — it exists so slice 2 (`svg-analyzer`) has
something real to classify instead of inline test strings.
